newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Wills sees good first qtr sales growth.
newsitem.headline: Wills sees good first qtr sales growth.

text.p: Cigarette manufacturer W.D. & H.O. Wills Ltd said on Wednesday it had continued to show good sales growth in the first quarter of 1997.

"Wills' sales revenue increased by 11 percent in 1996 and has continued to show good growth in the first quarter of 1997," Wills said in a statement responding to claims by competitors of a looming price war.
"Market share of our two flagship brands, Benson & Hedges and Horizon, continues to outperform the competition," Wills chief executive Stuart Watterton said in a statement.
He said he dismissed claims of a looming price war.
"I deplore the war-mongering statements of Mr Henry Goldberg, chief executive of Philip Morris, whose company continues to suffer as a result of Wills' growth," Watterton said.
Goldberg said in an interview published in The Australian newspaper on Wednesday that Wills had started a price war that would strip A$100 million from the sector's earnings in calendar 1997.
Goldberg also said he believed Wills would not make a profit in 1997.

"Whatever Mr Goldberg may say publicly, the fact remains that Philip Morris is the only company pursuing systematic discounting across the country in order to prop up its declining market share," Watterton said.
Philip Morris Australia had dropped the price of one of its leading brands on five seperate occasions during the last six months, Watterton said.
"It is obvious that Philip Morris' price discounting tactics are failing to halt the slide in their market share and revenue. Their attempts to provoke a price war only highlight their desperation."
Wills is due to hold their annual meeting on Thursday.
Watterton said Wills' performance had improved because of a restructuring of its trade marketing and distribution into specific teams and the introduction of a new in-store marketing concept.
He said Willis continued to keep its prices under review.
"We will not be provoked by our competitors. We will respond appropriately to any developments in the market in light of our competitive position and our desire to trade profitably," he said.
Wills, which is 67 percent owned by B.A.T. Industries, reported a A$13.27 million profit in calendar 1996, up from a loss of A$5.16 million in 1995, which was due to a price war two years ago.
Wills shares were 2.5 cents lower at A$2.05 at 10.45 a.m. (0045 GMT), having closed up 5.5 cents at A$2.075 on Tuesday.
